name: MarkuClean – AI Text Cleaner & Unicode Fixer
author: Ivijan-Stefan Stipic

sections.description:
MarkuClean is an AI text cleaner for WordPress. It removes AI-generated artifacts, invisible characters, broken Unicode sequences, and copy-and-paste leftovers from post titles, content, and excerpts. It works on text pasted from AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, and Grok, and on content copied from office documents, web pages, and PDFs.

You stay in control of when cleanup happens: while you paste in the editor, when content is displayed on the frontend, or when it is saved. Existing stored content is only modified when you enable Save Cleanup, and the built-in Tester lets you preview the result first. Defaults are sensible, so it works out of the box.

Need setup details, developer filters, or troubleshooting help? Read the full MarkuClean documentation.

What MarkuClean cleans

  • Invisible Unicode characters, including zero-width characters and non-breaking spaces
  • Mis-encoded smart quotes, dashes (including em dashes), and ellipses
  • Malformed encoding sequences and unwanted editor metadata
  • Numeric data-start/data-end markers and known AI attributes, including those found in Grok and Gemini responses
  • Known UTM tracking parameters in URLs inside sanitized HTML content
  • Copy-and-paste artifacts and malformed markup from AI writing tools, office documents, web pages, and PDFs

How it works

MarkuClean includes a paste cleaner for the Gutenberg editor, so AI-generated text is cleaned at the moment you paste it. Content edited in TinyMCE-based workflows is supported as well.

Display Cleanup cleans content only when it is displayed and never writes changes to the database. Save Cleanup updates stored content when enabled, and only when the content passes the built-in safety checks.

The Tester shows what would change without touching stored content. You can choose which post types are processed and add your own custom regular expression (regex) rules for project-specific cases.

Safe with page builders

Builder-managed content is skipped on purpose. Elementor, WPBakery / Visual Composer, Beaver Builder, Divi Builder, Oxygen, Bricks, SiteOrigin, and similar editors often store structured markup, shortcode trees, JSON-like payloads, or hidden metadata. MarkuClean returns that content unchanged.

Who it is for

Bloggers, editors, agencies, and developers who publish content drafted with AI tools or collected from external sources and want consistent, clean text without fixing every post by hand.

Documentation and support

Detailed guides are available in the MarkuClean documentation:

  • Settings and Cleanup Modes
  • Tester and Cleanup Examples
  • Content Safety and Page Builders
  • Developer API and WordPress Filters
  • Troubleshooting MarkuClean

Questions or bug reports are welcome in the support forum.
sections.installation:
Install from WordPress admin:

  1. Go to Plugins > Add New.
  2. Search for “MarkuClean”.
  3. Install and activate the plugin.

Manual installation:

  1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/.
  2. Activate the plugin in WordPress admin.
  3. Open Settings > AI Content Cleaner and configure the enabled post types and cleanup modes.
sections.faq:
How do I remove hidden characters from ChatGPT or other AI text in WordPress?

Activate MarkuClean, choose the post types you want to process, and paste your text into the editor. Invisible characters, broken Unicode, and known AI markup are cleaned according to your cleanup modes. Use the Tester to preview the result before enabling Save Cleanup on existing content.

Does it work with ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok output?

MarkuClean filters known AI attributes and markers from copied content, including numeric data-start/data-end markers and attributes found in Grok and Gemini responses. Results depend on how the source tool structures its HTML, so use the Tester to check your own content.

Can it replace em dashes, smart quotes, and ellipses?

Yes. Dashes, quotes, and ellipses are part of the configurable character replacements, and you can add your own regex rules. See the documentation for the available settings.

Does the plugin work with page builders?

Yes, where it is safe to do so. Some page builders store structured markup, shortcodes, JSON-like data, or internal metadata that should not be modified. When this content is detected, MarkuClean leaves it unchanged to help prevent unintended changes.

Does it work with the Classic Editor?

Yes. MarkuClean supports standard WordPress content edited in Gutenberg and TinyMCE-based workflows.

What characters does the plugin remove or normalize?

It can normalize configured character replacements, including mis-encoded quotes, dashes, ellipses, non-breaking spaces, zero-width characters, and other common copy-and-paste artifacts. It also removes numeric data-start/data-end markers and selected AI-generated text artifacts where supported.

Does it permanently modify existing content?

Only when Save Cleanup is enabled and the content passes the built-in safety checks. Display Cleanup and the Tester never modify stored content.

Can I limit cleanup to specific post types?

Yes. You can choose which post types are processed in the plugin settings. These settings apply consistently across supported frontend, editor, and save-time cleanup.

What is the difference between Display Cleanup and Save Cleanup?

Display Cleanup cleans content only when it is displayed and never writes changes to the database. Save Cleanup updates the stored content when enabled and the content passes the built-in safety checks.

Is it safe to use on live websites?

Yes. The plugin is designed to skip unsupported editing contexts and builder-managed content. Before enabling Save Cleanup for existing content, use the built-in Tester to review the results.

Where can I find the documentation?

The full documentation, including installation, settings, the Tester, Gutenberg integration, developer filters, and troubleshooting, is available at infinitumform.com/documentation/markuclean.
sections.changelog:
1.0.8

  • Added experimental Unicode normalization and mixed-script character cleanup, disabled by default.
  • Added new filters for Unicode normalization and character mappings.
  • Added Spanish (Chile), Russian, and Simplified Chinese translations (es_CL, ru_RU, zh_CN).

1.0.7

  • Site Health improvement

1.0.6

  • UX improvement

1.0.5

  • Fix: updated Gutenberg Paste Cleaner compatibility for the always-iframed post editor in WordPress 7.1.
  • Fix: paste handling now uses the active editor document for selection and insertion while preserving legacy editor behavior.
  • Added cleanup of known UTM tracking parameters from URLs in sanitized HTML content.

1.0.4

  • Added support for filtering out AI attributes from Grok and Gemini responses

1.0.3

  • Compatibility: prepared plugin metadata, editor assets, and readme for WordPress 7.0.
  • Compatibility: added backward-compatible Gutenberg sidebar fallback logic for both legacy and unified editor APIs.
  • Fix: aligned the activation PHP requirement check with the declared PHP 8.0 requirement.
  • Maintenance: replaced the non-standard dash in the plugin title with a standard hyphen.
  • Maintenance: verified plugin files against current WordPress coding and compatibility expectations without altering existing functionality.

1.0.2

  • Fix: prevent fatal errors with legacy WPBakery / Visual Composer on PHP 8.3
  • Fix: harden all WordPress hook callbacks against unexpected input types
  • Fix: ensure wp_insert_post_data callbacks are safe under legacy conditions
  • Improvement: extend legacy WPBakery / Visual Composer detection
  • Improvement: increase overall runtime compatibility with older plugins and themes

1.0.1

  • Fix: Save cleanup is now truly opt-in, no stored content is modified when disabled
  • Fix: Removed hardcoded “ChatGPT” text removal from sanitizer
  • Improvement: DOM cleanup now triggers only on structural AI/UI markers, not keywords
  • Fix: Prevent unintended content mutation in supported editors (Gutenberg, Classic)
  • Fix: Sidebar preview default value is now consistent across settings, UI, and runtime
  • Fix: Regex/replacement fields now preserve valid patterns (<, >, etc.)
  • Fix: PHP version requirement comment aligned with actual minimum version
  • Improvement: Updated admin UI examples to avoid misleading cleanup rules
  • Improvement: Increased overall sanitizer safety and reduced false-positive cleaning

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
